[L5] The span of a set is exactly the vectors obtained as finite linear combinations of its elements, including the empty combination. replacements.after:
[F4] The standard form is $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_{i<n}x_iy_i$ ([[def-standard-bilinear-form-on-a-coordinate-space]]).

[F5] Every vector in a span is a finite linear combination of the spanning vectors, and the empty span is the zero subspace. In particular, a finite basis expresses every vector of its space as a finite combination. ([[lem-span-is-the-set-of-linear-combinations]])

[F6] The standard coordinate basis gives $\dim_F F^n=n$, including $n=0$ and its empty basis. ([[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]])

2.1 If $x\in\ker\Phi$, its pairing with every basis vector $u_i$ is zero. For every $u\in U$, [F1] and [F5] express $u$ as a finite linear combination of these basis vectors, so bilinearity [F4] gives $\langle x,u\rangle=0$. Conversely, $x\in U^\perp$ pairs to zero with every $u_i\in U$, so $\Phi(x)=0$. Thus $\ker\Phi=U^\perp$, including $d=0$ when all combinations and coordinate equations are empty.
